label: Transformer (causal encoder over daily tokens)

compute.eval_note: harness evaluate.py per rung (800 sim val runs + 52 dev basins) not included: about 0.5-4 CPU-min per rung
compute.notes: 4 rungs; one thread (torch.set_num_threads(1)), time.process_time() of the training process, shared 2-core machine

feature_engineering: None beyond the shared arms_seq pipeline (common/seqlib.py), identical for all four sequence arms: FlowCast's 11 scaled daily features (P/10, log1p P, PET/5, T_mean/T_min/T_max /10, SRAD/150, vp/1000, wind/3, sin/cos day of year) + FlowCast's 18-value static vector (batch["static"], standardised with the train bank mean/sd) repeated every day; target in units of the basin mean precipitation exp(static[11]); 730-day windows (365 warm-up + 365 target), inference in 365-day blocks each with its own 365-day warm-up (FlowCast). Causal: day t uses forcing up to day t only.
rule: keep if sim val median NSE (all 800 frozen runs) > incumbent + 0.01 AND dev median NSE (52 dev basins, WY2001-2014) >= 0.95 x incumbent's

rungs.change: base: daily tokens, FlowCast's training recipe (3000 steps)
rungs.why: first rung; learns slowly (quick val 0.30 / 0.34 / 0.39 at 1k / 2k / 3k steps vs the LSTM's 0.38 / 0.40 / 0.45).
sim +0.037 over r0 (paired bootstrap +0.016..+0.053) and dev 0.389 >= 0.95 x 0.362: kept (superseded by r3).

rungs.change: causal 7-day patches (105 tokens, 2 blocks): each day reads the attention output of all earlier complete weeks + a depthwise causal conv over its own last 7 days; 25.8k parameters; 6000 steps
rungs.why: sim 0.341 vs incumbent r1 0.401: weekly tokens lose more than they save (10x cheaper per step).

rungs.change: r1 with 2x training (12000 steps, cosine over 12000) and 2 attention heads of size 16 instead of 4 of size 8 (same 26.9k parameters; halves the attention cost so the run fits the 4 CPU-hour budget)
rungs.why: sim 0.4205 vs incumbent r1 0.4008 (+0.020; paired bootstrap +0.002..+0.032) and dev 0.411 >= 0.95 x 0.389 (dev +0.022, CI -0.028..+0.047): kept. Released (last rung). Two changes in one rung (steps and heads), so the gain cannot be split between them; the LSTM's 12000-step rung gained only +0.003, so most of it is probably the transformer's slower learning catching up.

export_check.note: numpy float64 (released predict.py) vs torch float32 (training checkpoint), mm/day, 16 sim val windows + 3 dev basins (14 years each)

bands: raw pinball quantiles (no dev widening; arm C conformalises every arm)
